As of the as-of date of 2020-01-01, the document timeline only includes rules in force on or before 2020-01-01. The relevant rule for the acquisition limit within a financial year for an acquirer holding 25% or more is Regulation 3(2), which states that an acquirer holding 25% or more but less than the maximum permissible non-public shareholding shall not acquire within any financial year additional shares or voting rights entitling them to exercise more than 5% of the voting rights without making an open offer ("No acquirer who together with persons acting in concert holds 25% or more but less than the maximum permissible non-public shareholding, shall acquire within any financial year additional shares or voting rights entitling them to exercise more than five per cent of the voting rights, unless an open offer is made."). Given 10 crore total shares outstanding, acquiring more than 5% of the voting rights corresponds to 5% of 10 crore shares = 0.5 crore shares (or 50,000,000 shares). Therefore, the maximum number of additional shares they can acquire without triggering a mandatory open offer is up to 5% of the voting rights, which is 0.5 crore shares.

citations.quote: No acquirer who together with persons acting in concert holds 25% or more but less than the maximum permissible non-public shareholding, shall acquire within any financial year additional shares or voting rights entitling them to exercise more than five per cent of the voting rights, unless an open offer is made.

answer: As of 2020-01-01, before ordering an inspection, SEBI must give not less than ten days notice to the investment adviser. SEBI can dispense with this notice under the circumstance where the Board is satisfied that in the interest of the investors no such notice should be given, and it may by an order in writing direct that the inspection be taken up without such notice.

citations.quote: Regulation 24(1): Before ordering an inspection under regulation 23, the Board shall give not less than ten days notice to the investment adviser. (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-regulation (1), where the Board is satisfied that in the interest of the investors no such notice should be given, it may by an order in writing direct that the inspection of the affairs of the investment adviser be taken up without such notice.

answer: According to Securities and exchange board of india credit rating ag (in force since 1999-01-01): "Regulation 5(l) (inserted by SEBI (CRA) (Amendment) Regulations, 2018, w.e.f. 30-05-2018): the promoter of the credit rating agency, in terms of regulation 4, has a minimum shareholding of 26% in the credit rating agency."
